evidence:
Read the actual frozen rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx with openpyxl: Quality Checks row 27 (number 26) requires 'Every requirement the prompt states maps to at least one criterion'; Internal Quality Checks row 27 explains that multiple verifiers may share a flow. Applied frozen Harbor SKILL.md, references/quality-checks.md:112-114 and qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md's coverage correction. Paths below are relative to .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/task unless stated otherwise. Parsed all five judge.toml files: Render 1 criterion, Constraints 1, Functional 64, Polish 7, Visual 6. The product-behavior map is extensive: instruction.md:1,7 and overview.md:3-9 map to Render plus Functional startup_ready, usable_examples, example_separate and saved_record_fidelity; behaviour.md:5 maps to js_html_filename_dispatch, css_apply_snapshot, extension_case, js_fresh_document, css_inert_copy and css_pending_timer_cancelled; behaviour.md:7-13 maps to later_interactions, completed_stop, supersede_pending, stop_pending_execution/rollback, literal_loop_deadline/rollback and callback_shared_run_deadline/timeout_rollback; behaviour.md:15 maps to the JS, HTML, timer and Promise message/line/rollback/recovery outcomes, with exact fixtures in functional/prompt.md:S10-S13; behaviour.md:19 maps to console_level_stream, console_value_inspection, console_history, console_duration, console_clear_control and terminal_durations; behaviour.md:21 maps to the three Auto-run outcomes plus manual_run_independent_of_autorun; behaviour.md:25-29 maps to saved_record_fidelity, saved_records_browser_reload, the four title outcomes, stale_save_server_refusal and stale_save_draft_recovery. Integration.md:7's observable durability/no-duplication promise maps to S22's process_restart_durability and process_restart_write. security.md:3-11 maps to preview_origin_boundary, the supported literal and callback tests, harmless_scope_words, unsupported_execution_refused, snippet_network_boundary and save_load_execution_canary; representative browser canaries are evidence of those promises, not exhaustive proofs. ui.md:3-9 maps to editor_monospace/line_numbers/syntax_colouring, both theme outcomes, all seven Polish criteria and the six Visual criteria. Shared scenarios were not treated as gaps, and separately useful outcomes retain their own criteria.

Confirmed source-level coverage mismatch: environment/instructions/integration.md:11 mandates 'Use Express, better-sqlite3 and Node built-ins for the one server process, without an external backend or database service'; policy.md:7 additionally says the saved library belongs to the local 'SQLite database'. Constraints explicitly declines to establish this: tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:29 says 'This gate establishes a basic shared server write/read, not SQLite or Express specifically.' Its prompt.md:6-11 prohibits implementation/database-file inspection and :20-21 says never infer a particular database engine. Functional prompt.md:7 likewise forbids source, bundles and database-byte inspection; all of its 64 descriptions were checked and none grades the prescribed backend stack or absence of an external server-side data service. S22:409-415 establishes durable read/write behavior, which also works with a JSON-file backend or an external service. tests/test.sh:68-111 enforces an entry file, link boundaries and Node launch, but never inspects/enforces the backend engine or package use. This is an inherited contract conflict, not a demand to alter the canonical harness: frozen rules/projects/webdev-task-template/environment/instructions/integration.md:3-9 prescribes the same Node/Express/better-sqlite3/SQLite runtime, and :12-14 disallows an external backend.

The same browser-only coverage boundary leaves task-added artifact promises without an owner: instruction.md:9 asks to 'Include the source and built frontend'; integration.md:5 requires UI served from '/app/public/index.html', and :11 requires compiled application scripts/styles and says startup 'mustn't install packages'. Neither the five criterion files nor the inspected test.sh checks source delivery, that exact frontend artifact location, build inclusion, or startup installation. Serving equivalent assets directly from server.js, shipping only a compiled bundle without its authoring source, or an otherwise fast successful startup installation can produce the same observed browser results. These are delivery obligations, not absent playground features; their bounded nature is why this is P2 rather than a claim that execution/library coverage is broadly missing. No source or canonical settings were changed.

Conforming-alternative check: integration.md:3 makes React/TypeScript/Vite optional. A vanilla frontend, server-rendered library responses, an optional language indicator, proactive stale-save prevention with retained dirty fields, a static restored last-good preview and a narrow stacked layout are explicitly accepted by the relevant prompts/criteria, so these are not coverage or false-failure findings. The raw-evidence index states that available runs are scripted browser observations, not configured judge/model measurements. This report establishes the mapping defect by source inspection only; the counterexample was not executed and no empirical reward is claimed.
counterexample: A submission keeps the same fully working playground frontend and implements the same API with Node's built-in HTTP server and an atomically written JSON file at DB_PATH, including exact fields, durable identities, revisions and conflict checks. It answers health, shares records across clean contexts, survives process restart, and produces every requested browser observation, so no defined criterion distinguishes it from the mandated Express/better-sqlite3/SQLite implementation. It nevertheless violates integration.md:11 and policy.md:7. Separately, serving the identical frontend bytes from an in-memory HTML string without /app/public/index.html, or delivering built bytes without authoring source, violates explicit delivery instructions while leaving all browser criteria unchanged. These are plausible source-derived witnesses, not measured mutation runs.
suggested_fix: Have the shared-profile owner reconcile mandatory backend/runtime and artifact obligations with the browser-only grading policy: document them as environment guidance if they are not graded, or provide an approved deterministic contract check; remove unnecessary task-added artifact prescriptions only where authorized. Do not silently change canonical harness files or add private-source reading to browser judges.
